ppi_focus: Confirm 5-speed vs SMT. On a 5-speed, check clutch engagement height and slip in 4th/5th, and shift-cable bushing slop.
Engine: compression and leak-down, borescope all four bores, and inspect plugs for oil fouling.
Exhaust manifold and pre-cat rattle on cold start; full OBD-II scan including readiness monitors for P0420/P0421.
Coolant system pressure test, including the long underbody steel pipes, clamps, radiator and hoses.
Underside on a lift: jack points, rockers, front subframe and rear suspension mounts.
Suspension bushings, ball joints, end links and dampers; engine and transaxle mounts for driveline clunk.
ABS and EPS: scan for stored codes and test steering effort.
Front wheel arch and door areas: paint meter for repaint or filler.
Soft top seals, rear bulkhead drains and footwell dampness.
Tire date codes and condition; brake fluid condition and rear pad thickness.
what_would_change_verdict: Up: photo confirmation of the 5-speed C56, a clutch replacement invoice, and a measured oil-consumption result of about a quart per 3,000+ miles or better.
Up: a clean PPI with good compression, no catalyst codes and dry coolant pipes, plus service records showing cooling-system work.
Down: the car is an SMT, or shows heavy oil consumption, blue smoke or pre-cat rattle.
Down: the paint meter reveals accident repair beyond the disclosed cosmetics, or underbody corrosion appears on the coolant pipes or jack points.
Down: the seller declines a PPI or cannot supply a smog certificate.
evidence.mission_note: If it is confirmed as the 5-speed, this is a cheap, simple, mid-engine manual roadster well below the ideal budget band and easy to resell within 6–24 months, a reasonable enthusiast bridge while the RX covers daily duty. If it is the SMT, it does not satisfy the manual requirement.
evidence.rationale: The listing establishes identity well: a published VIN decoding cleanly to a 2003 ZZW30 1.8L convertible, a clean-title claim and a $9,500 price that matches the mileage-adjusted fair value of about $9,754. Photos show a straight, stock-looking silver facelift car with new headlights, an intact-looking top with the glass rear window and decent tread. The seller discloses cosmetic faults: driver-seat upholstery, door dents, a bumper scratch and the antenna. A paint scuff at the trailing edge of the front wheel arch is also visible. Nothing in the captured text documents the model-critical items at 128,664 miles: oil consumption, clutch history, pre-cat condition or the underbody coolant pipes. Capture was thin, so records may exist but were not seen. The single most consequential open fact is whether 'Manual transmission' means the C56 5-speed or the SMT, because that decides mission eligibility and a large share of the risk profile.
evidence.next_action: Message the seller asking for a photo of the pedals and shifter to confirm 5-speed vs SMT, tire date codes, any oil and clutch records, and agreement to a PPI at an independent shop near Glendale.
